text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.85% today as oil prices held steady in the mid-$90s globally and the mid-$89s domestically. The stock had dropped sharply on November 23rd following the collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, which failed to include fossil fuel phase-out language—a symbolic win for the energy sector that removed near-term regulatory risk. Today's rebound reflects both stabilization after that selloff and the absence of fresh negative headlines.

Regional geopolitical tensions—Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and ongoing strikes on Russian refineries—keep underlying energy prices supported, which benefits a major crude producer like ConocoPhillips even without directional movement in the broader oil market.
